sourceContext: Human requires clean deterministic organization for every Codex thread/task: short task-linked names, project-scoped storage, automatic project/task folder creation, and no anonymous/random chat names. This command supersedes command 03 and keeps all prior safe productization authority while correcting project identity and organization.
objective: Finish ORCHESTOR as a standalone installable multi-project/multi-task agent with deterministic project/task/thread organization. Every task must have a short human-readable name, a project-specific folder and a durable thread binding; anonymous/random chat names are forbidden.
why: The user wants ORCHESTOR to remain orderly as projects and concurrent tasks grow. Thread/task identity must be human-readable and physically/logically grouped by project from the start.
scope: Treat ORCHESTOR itself as its own project identity: projectId=orchestor. The Costa Clean repository may remain a temporary control-plane transport only; it is not the ORCHESTOR project identity.
Current ORCHESTOR source root is C:\Users\USUARIO\orchestor.
Create/use a global per-user ORCHESTOR home outside product repositories. Preferred Windows path: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Orchestor.
For every registered project create a deterministic project directory if missing: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Orchestor\projects\<projectSlug>\.
Inside each project keep distinct subdirectories for tasks, workstreams, threads, runs, locks, logs, results and cache. Runtime state must never be scattered into unrelated repositories.

For every new task create a short human-readable task slug and display name derived from the actual objective. Random UUIDs may exist internally only as IDs, never as the primary visible task/thread name.
For this task the canonical visible name is `ORCHESTOR Core` and canonical task/workstream slug is `core-productization`.
Preferred current task folder: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Orchestor\projects\orchestor\tasks\core-productization\.

Persist thread metadata inside the project/task hierarchy, including projectId, task/workstreamId, displayName, threadId, runId(s), repositoryRoot, worktreeRoot, branch, status, createdAt and updatedAt.
When creating a new Codex app-server thread, set its human-readable title/name to the task display name if the app-server supports thread renaming/title metadata.

If Codex app-server does not support a real thread title/folder primitive, do not fake it. Persist the canonical display name and folder organization in ORCHESTOR and surface that name in the ORCHESTOR UI/dashboard; document the platform limitation.
Never create a new task/thread with a meaningless visible name such as random UUID, 'new chat', 'thread 1', or an arbitrary X.
Thread naming must be concise: normally 2-5 words, unique within the project when necessary by a small semantic suffix, not by long hashes.
On project registration, auto-create the project folder hierarchy if absent. On task creation, auto-create the task folder and metadata atomically before dispatch.
All task lanes must remain isolated by project folder, task folder, thread binding, run state, worktree and locks.

Continue all productization requirements from CC-ORCHESTOR-PRODUCTIZE-20260930-03: safe thread bootstrap, FIRST_DISPATCH, autonomous loop, zero visible windows, ON/OFF/PAUSED/NEEDS_YOU UX, multi-project/multi-task concurrency, conflict serialization, restart recovery, notifications, packaging and E2E certification.

For the current ORCHESTOR task, inspect for an existing valid thread first. Reuse it only if ownership can be proven and its canonical ORCHESTOR metadata can be attached to projectId=orchestor/workstreamId=core-productization without ambiguity.
If no valid existing thread exists, create exactly one new persistent Codex app-server thread and register it as displayName=`ORCHESTOR Core` under the ORCHESTOR project/task folder.
Superseded Costa Clean-scoped orchestrator-core thread/run bindings must be preserved as historical evidence and must not remain the active project identity.
Create exactly one active durable run for this command after the project/task/thread binding is valid.
Perform FIRST_DISPATCH and continue autonomously until PROJECT_COMPLETE=YES or a genuine human safety gate.
Do not modify Costa Clean application/product source.
outOfScope: Secrets, DNS, billing, payments, real external communications or destructive remote actions.
Direct OpenAI API or OPENAI_API_KEY usage.
Pretending Codex has native folder/title capabilities if the app-server does not expose them.
acceptanceCriteria: ORCHESTOR project identity is independent from Costa Clean: projectId=orchestor.
Global ORCHESTOR home exists outside repositories and project-specific folders are auto-created.
Current task has visible name `ORCHESTOR Core` and folder `projects/orchestor/tasks/core-productization` (platform-normalized equivalent acceptable).
Every task/thread binding has a short human-readable displayName plus durable project/task metadata.
Anonymous/random visible thread names are not used.
If Codex native title support exists it is used; otherwise ORCHESTOR UI/metadata presents the canonical task name and the limitation is documented.
Exactly one valid persistent thread is active for ORCHESTOR Core.
Exactly one active run exists for this command.
All command 03 productization acceptance criteria remain in force.
Costa Clean application source mutations=0 and production/Supabase remote mutations=0.
requiredApprovals: Any Supabase or other remote database mutation.
Any secret/credential creation, rotation or disclosure.
Any DNS, billing, payment or real external communication.
Any material expansion beyond ORCHESTOR productization and non-production certification.
stopConditions: More than one ambiguous candidate active thread cannot be safely disambiguated.
A second new active thread would be required for the same task.
Zero-visible-window behavior regresses and cannot be safely repaired.
A forbidden or approval-required real-world side effect becomes necessary.
Bounded no-progress guards are exhausted with unresolved correctness/security findings.
verificationRequirements: Report whether native Codex thread naming is SUPPORTED or UNSUPPORTED.
Prove no random visible thread names were created.
Prove project/task folders and metadata are isolated from other repos/tasks.
Continue and complete all final productization verification from command 03.

Final report must include PROJECT_COMPLETE, INSTALLABLE_AGENT, UI_STATE_MODEL, MULTI_PROJECT, MULTI_TASK, TASK_NAMING, PROJECT_FOLDER_ISOLATION, CONFLICT_SERIALIZATION, MANUAL_COPY_PASTE_REQUIRED, ZERO_VISIBLE_WINDOWS, THREAD_POLICY, REVIEW_REPAIR_LOOP, RESTART_RECOVERY, HUMAN_GATES, NOTIFICATIONS, TESTS, FINAL_CERTIFICATION, APP_SOURCE_MUTATIONS, PRODUCTION_MUTATIONS and REMAINING_BLOCKERS.
